newsitem.title: USA: Dole closes gap slightly to 11.9 pct - Reuters poll.
newsitem.headline: Dole closes gap slightly to 11.9 pct - Reuters poll.

text.p: Republican challenger Bob Dole continued to whittle away at President Bill Clinton's lead ahead of the Nov. 5 election, narrowing the gap to 11.9 percentage points in Thursday's Reuters tracking poll.

The poll, taken before Wednesday's nationally televised presidential debate, showed Democrat Clinton at 45 percent, compared with Dole's 33.1 percent and Reform Party candidate Ross Perot's 6.3 percent. Two and a half percent chose "other" and 13.1 percent were undecided.
On Wednesday the poll, conducted for Reuters by John Zogby Group International, showed Clinton with a 12.8 point lead.
"These new figures essentially show Clinton dropping, but Dole staying fixed in the low to mid-30s as he has been throughout almost all of our tracking," pollster John Zogby said .

He said that while Dole has apparently made some gains in Western states, he managed to capture just three out of four Republicans and six out of 10 voters who believe the country is on the "wrong track".

By contrast, Clinton leads among those who live in households where someone has lost a job in the past year, is working at a job that pays less, and is afraid of losing a job in the next year, Zogby said.

The Reuters/Zogby poll tracks about 900 likely voters over a three-day period. The latest result, with a 3.3 percentage point margin of error, is a rolling average of polling from Monday through Wednesday, but before the Wednesday evening debate.
Zogby said the poll released on Friday's would begin to reflect the impact of the debate.

The race for Congress showed a widening margin for the Democrats, with 39.1 percent of respondents saying they will vote for the Democratic candidate in their district compared with 32.7 percent who say they plan to choose the Republican.

Those polled prefer a Democratic Senate majority by a slim margin, with 40.5 percent choosing the Democrats over 38.9 percent who want a Republican Senate majority, while voters who prefer the Democrats to lead the next House of Representatives widened their lead to 41 percent over the 37.6 percent who prefer a House Republican majority.
Just under half, or 49.2 percent, believe Clinton
deserves re-election, compared with 39.4 percent who do not.
